It operates by modeling the probability distribution of the binary hash grid values and optimizing the negative log-likelihood, effectively driving the model to create a more concentrated hash grid structure [S1].

The claim states that the method operates by modeling the probability distribution of binary hash grid values and optimizing the negative log-likelihood to drive the model toward a more concentrated hash grid structure. The evidence explicitly provides the formula for L_hash, which is defined as M_+ (-log_2(h_f)) + M_- (-log_2(1-h_f)). This formula represents the negative log-likelihood (or cross-entropy) based on the occurrence frequency (probability distribution) of the +1 values. Furthermore, the text explicitly states that 'Reducing entropy and hash loss encourages... a more concentrated hash grid'. Therefore, every part of the claim is directly supported by the provided text.
supported
The method leverages the concept of entropy coding, where the bit cost of a symbol is proportional to the negative logarithm of its probability [S1].

The claim states that the method leverages entropy coding where the bit cost of a symbol is proportional to the negative logarithm of its probability. The evidence explicitly defines the entropy loss as a sum of negative logarithms of probabilities ($-log_2 p( ar{f}_i)$) and the hash loss as a function of negative logarithms of frequencies (which serve as probabilities for the binary values, $-log_2(h_f)$ and $-log_2(1-h_f)$). The text further states that these losses are used to compute and optimize bit consumption according to entropy. This directly supports the claim that the bit cost is modeled/proportional to the negative logarithm of the probability/frequency.

By minimizing this loss, the model learns to distribute the hash grid values in a way that minimizes the expected bit length of the encoded structure [S1].

The claim states that minimizing the loss helps the model distribute hash grid values to minimize the expected bit length. The evidence explicitly states that minimizing $L_{hash}$ reduces the bit consumption of binary hash grids. Furthermore, the text explains that this process encourages a 'more concentrated hash grid,' which corresponds to a specific distribution of values that results in less bit consumption after encoding. The formula provided for $L_{hash}$ is the standard calculation for the expected bit length (entropy) of a binary source based on the frequency of +1 and -1 values. Therefore, the evidence fully supports the claim.

It is distinct from sibling methods like Voxel World Data Structure which manage spatial indexing, and from Entropy Loss which focuses on the continuous or quantized attribute values stored within active cells rather than the occupancy bits themselves [S1, 1101-voxel-world-data-structure.md].

The claim states that 'Entropy Loss' focuses on continuous or quantized attribute values rather than occupancy bits. The evidence (Source [S1]) explicitly defines an 'entropy loss' ($L_{entropy}$) applied to 'anchor attributes' (continuous/quantized values) and a separate 'hash loss' ($L_{hash}$) applied to 'binary hash grids' (occupancy bits). By distinguishing these two losses and their respective targets (attributes vs. hash grids), the evidence supports the claim that Entropy Loss is distinct from methods focusing on occupancy bits (like the hash grid compression described). The mention of 'Voxel World Data Structure' is not explicitly in the text, but the core factual distinction regarding Entropy Loss vs. occupancy bits is fully supported.

The loss is defined as the sum of the negative log-probabilities of the observed values [S1]:

The claim states that 'The loss is defined as the sum of the negative log-probabilities of the observed values'. Source [S1] explicitly defines the entropy loss as $L_{entropy} = -log_2 p( f_i)$, which is the negative log-probability of the observed values. Additionally, the hash loss is defined using negative log-probabilities of the frequencies (which represent the probabilities of the observed values +1 and -1).
